title: Tiger Woods to change not guilty plea in DUI case, court records show
content:
Court records show that Tiger Woods plans to change his not guilty plea in his DUI case in Florida.

Woods’ attorney, Douglas Duncan, filed a document with Martin County Court on Tuesday calling for a change of plea hearing on Wednesday in front of Judge Darren Steele. The hearing is scheduled to begin at 8:30 a.m. local time.

The hearing comes days ahead of a scheduled docket sounding, which is a pre-trial court hearing in which a judge checks with both sides to see if they’re ready for trial, need a delay, or have reached a plea deal. The docket sounding is scheduled for Sept. 8.

The DUI case stems from a crash on March 27 in which Woods, 50, clipped a pickup truck with his vehicle, causing his car to roll over. Neither Woods nor the driver of the truck reported injuries from the crash. Woods told police that he looked down at his cellphone and was changing the radio station when the crash occurred. He was arrested after he failed a sobriety test. While the breathalyzer test showed no traces of alcohol, Woods refused to take a urine test, and according to officers, admitted to taking “a few pills.” Two hydrocodone pills were later found in Woods’ pocket, according to an arrest affidavit released by the Martin County Sheriff’s Office and reviewed by The Athletic. Officers described Woods as “lethargic.” Woods was subsequently charged with driving under the influence with property damage and refusal to submit to a lawful urinalysis test.

Woods’ attorney, Duncan, pleaded not guilty to both charges on the golfer’s behalf on March 31 and demanded a jury trial. On the same day, Woods announced that he was “stepping away” for an undisclosed period of time to “seek treatment.” He was allowed to leave the country, spending weeks at a rehab facility in Switzerland.

In April, prosecutors filed a motion for subpoena in which they said they would seek information from Lewis Pharmacy regarding any medication prescribed to Woods from the start of 2026 until March 27, the day of the crash in Jupiter Island, where he has a home. According to the court filing, prosecutors sought information including “date and time prescription was filled, type of prescription, number of pills in each prescription, the dosage amount, all special instructions on how to take the medication, date of next refill, all warnings, including but not limited to operating a motor vehicle while taking the prescription.”

Duncan objected to the state’s request for a subpoena and asked the court to conduct a hearing to determine if the prescription records were “relevant to a criminal investigation.” But at a hearing in May, Judge Steele granted the state’s request for access to Woods’ prescription drug records.

Duncan is the same attorney who represented Woods in his 2017 DUI arrest. Woods completed a DUI diversion program after pleading guilty to a reckless driving charge. He was placed on probation and had to serve 50 hours of community service.

In 2009, Woods spent 45 days in an inpatient clinic after news of multiple affairs came to light, shocking the sports world.

— Hugh Kellenberger, Gabby Herzig and Brody Miller contributed to this story.
